title: The Gumagan
summary: The Mokole of Australia and its islands.

claims.text: Gumagan are wereSaurians of Bandaiyan, born to native peoples of Oceania, whose reptile forms are saltwater crocodiles or perenties, giant lizards kin to the Komodo dragon.
Alone among the Mokole, they hold the Sun to be female, a Great Mother, and the Moon male, as their Aboriginal neighbours do, and they recognise seven solar auspices.
They revere the Dreamtime ancestors who made the world and became it; the Bunyip, once their teachers in Umbral travel, were wiped out after the coming of Europeans and Garou.
Gumagan live in the deserts, Arnhem Land, New Guinea and the Torres Strait Islands; none have been left in southern Australia since the war that began in 1788.

title: The Makara
summary: The Mokole of India and their seasonal auspices.

claims.text: Makara divide their auspices by season, not hour: Hemanta of winter are tricksters, Zarad of autumn mystics, Grisma of summer judges and police, Vasanta of spring warriors and travellers.
They see themselves as the diplomat stream of the Mokole, bound to aid the other children of their Mother.
Their great forms grow from the dreams of the Wani, the ancient Dragon Princes, ranging from vast crocodiles to many-headed serpents and Eastern dragons.
Zhong Lung great forms look more like dragons than any other Mokole's, with the nine resemblances, gills, manes and fiery pearls.
The War of Rage never reached the Middle Kingdom, so they do not hate the Hakken the way African Mokole hate Garou; their foes are the Kuei-jin and other things of Yomi.
In mixed sentai they often serve as Pillars and Fists, and other hengeyokai treat them with clear awe.
Few remain, but they live long, through the Sleep of the Dragon, elixirs and the shedding of old skin and bone; their Kin once fed and worshipped them for bringing rain.

title: Lost and Devoured Memories
summary: Spirits tied to the Mokole gift of ancestral memory.

claims.text: Mokole can walk into any memory held by their kind and play out its story; changing a remembered event is very hard, and a whole army might fail to rewrite a great moment of history.
Makara call a Mokole who has lost all memory pranastajjanika, a fate worse than death, and believe a spirit called a Pratigata holds that lost memory and could restore it.
Smrtihara are Deep Umbra spirits that devour Gaia's memories; some Makara call them daughters of the Demoness of Sorrow, born of the world's suicidal imbalance.
